about.title: Coronado Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death results from someone else's negligence, California law gives certain family members the right to seek compensation through a wrongful death claim. In Coronado, a small island city bordered by the Silver Strand and threaded by corridors like Orange Avenue, 4th Street, and 3rd Street, most reported collisions in the latest full year involved injuries rather than fatalities, with Fridays in the mid-afternoon showing the most reports. Wrongful death cases aren't limited to roadway crashes, though. They can arise from premises negligence at a hotel or resort, a boating incident along the bay, a medical error, or a defective product. Because California limits who may bring these claims and sets a strict filing deadline, families often benefit from talking to an attorney early. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney in our network who can walk through your options and explain what may be recoverable under the circumstances.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing primarily to a spouse, domestic partner, or children, with other dependents or heirs eligible in certain situations. An attorney can help determine who in your family qualifies to bring the claim.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Starts at Death
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims in California must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Acting early preserves evidence and keeps your options open.

items.title: Losses Go Beyond Funeral Costs
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral and burial expenses, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. These claims are civil matters, separate from any related criminal proceeding.

items.question: The recent crash data for Coronado shows no traffic deaths that year. Does that mean wrongful death claims don't apply here?
items.answer: Not at all. Public crash records reflect one year of roadway data and don't capture every circumstance that can lead to a wrongful death claim, such as incidents on the water, at a business, or in a medical setting. If your family lost someone due to another party's negligence, an independent attorney can evaluate whether a claim may apply.

items.question: Who in the family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Typically, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible under California law. An attorney can review your family's specific situation to clarify who has standing.

items.question: How long do we have to file a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: In most cases, California allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a city agency, may be involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate notice process. Speaking with an attorney soon after a loss helps protect your family's ability to act within these timeframes.
